Chapter overview

Contemporary Tamil literature moves from post-Independence free verse and mature fiction to regional, Dalit, feminist, Sri Lankan and diaspora writing, experimental theatre, little magazines, translations and global recognition.

Post-Independence contextPoetryFictionNew voicesTheatre & journalsRecognition
Period, Scope and Post-Independence Literary Context

Contemporary Tamil literature is framed through post-Independence transformation, new political and social movements, migration, diaspora and twenty-first-century media.

Period and Scope

For this syllabus, contemporary Tamil literature mainly covers developments from the 1960s and 1970s to the present.

The major areas are:

  • Puthu Kavithai or free verse
  • Literary modernism
  • Postmodern fiction
  • Regional literature
  • Dalit literature
  • Feminist literature
  • Sri Lankan and diaspora writing
  • Contemporary drama
  • Literary journals
  • Major awards and author–work associations

Tamil Virtual Academy classifies the growth of modern Tamil poetry through the Manikkodi, Ezhuthu and Vaanambadi phases.

Contemporary Tamil literature is studied here mainly as a post-Independence and late-twentieth-century development extending into the twenty-first century.

Its background includes urbanisation, industrialisation, migration, Dravidian politics, Marxist thought, Dalit assertion, feminist thought, the Sri Lankan Tamil experience and the growth of a global Tamil diaspora.

New poetry, fiction and drama responded to changing social structures, new media, political movements and expanding regional and international readerships.

Puthu Kavithai is introduced here only as one major development; its movement, journals and principal pioneer are treated in the next topic.

Puthu Kavithai Movement and Na. Pichamurthy

Puthu Kavithai developed as a sustained free-verse movement through journals, modern speech, world-poetry influences and Na. Pichamurthy’s pioneering role.

Puthu Kavithai

Puthu Kavithai refers to modern Tamil free verse.

Other terms used include:

  • Vasana Kavithai
  • Yappilla Kavithai
  • Kattillada Kavithai

Subramania Bharati experimented with prose poetry, while Na. Pichamurthy became an important pioneer of modern Tamil free verse.

Contemporary poetry reduced dependence on traditional Yappu rules and adopted conversational language, imagery, symbolism and flexible line arrangements.

Free verse encouraged colloquial language, individual experience, urban observation, social criticism and engagement with world poetry.

Literary journals helped establish Puthu Kavithai as a sustained movement rather than an isolated formal experiment.

Three Phases of Modern Tamil Poetry
Manikkodi Phase

Associated with literary experimentation during the 1930s.

Important writers included:

  • Na. Pichamurthy
  • Pudhumaipithan
  • Ku. Pa. Rajagopalan
  • Mouni
Ezhuthu Phase

The literary journal Ezhuthu was founded by C. S. Chellappa in January 1959.

It promoted:

  • Puthu Kavithai
  • Literary criticism
  • Modernist fiction
  • Experimental writing

Important poets associated with this phase included:

  • Na. Pichamurthy
  • C. Mani
  • Nakulan
  • Pramil
  • Pasuvayya

Ezhuthu became a major platform for modern Tamil poetry and criticism.

Vaanambadi Phase

The Vaanambadi poetry movement became prominent during the 1970s.

Important poets associated with the broader phase include:

  • Sirpi Balasubramaniam
  • Abdul Rahman
  • Mu. Metha
  • Tamilanban
  • Puviyarasu
  • Meera
  • Inkulab

The movement gave prominence to social issues, labour, equality, humanism and accessible poetic language.

Na. Pichamurthy

Na. Pichamurthy was an important pioneer of Puthu Kavithai.

He was also associated with:

  • Manikkodi
  • Short stories
  • Essays
  • Psychological writing

His poetry departed from strict traditional metres and used modern images and individual experience.

His significance in this chapter lies primarily in the development of free verse and the transition from the Manikkodi environment to later modernist poetry; Chapter 7 treats his early short-story context concisely.

Pramil, Nakulan and Gnanakoothan

Pramil, Nakulan and Gnanakoothan represent distinct modernist directions in symbolism, psychological experiment, satire and urban observation.

Pramil

Original name: Dharmu Sivaramu

Pen name: Pramil

Pramil was an important modernist Tamil poet.

His poetry is associated with:

  • Dense imagery
  • Symbolism
  • Individual consciousness
  • Philosophical inquiry
  • Experimental language

He also wrote literary criticism and essays.

His dense modernist poetry often requires interpretation through image, symbol and philosophical association rather than direct narration.

Nakulan

Original name: T. K. Doraiswamy

Pen name: Nakulan

Nakulan contributed to:

  • Poetry
  • Novels
  • Short stories
  • Translation
  • Literary criticism

Important works include:

  • Ninaivuppathai
  • Naigal
  • Naveenan Diary
  • Sila Athiyayangal

His writing is associated with modernism, memory, identity and psychological experimentation.

His fiction and poetry are associated with stream-of-consciousness techniques, modern alienation and experiments in narrative voice.

Gnanakoothan

Important poetry collections include:

  • Andru Veru Kizhamai
  • Sooriyanukku Pin Pakkam

His poetry is known for:

  • Irony
  • Satire
  • Ordinary urban situations
  • Political observation
  • Concise language

He used everyday speech and compressed humour to expose political and urban contradictions.

Abdul Rahman, Mu. Metha and Sirpi

Abdul Rahman, Mu. Metha and Sirpi combined modern imagery with humanism, accessible language, rural life and social consciousness.

Abdul Rahman

Popular title: Kavikko

Important works include:

  • Paal Veethi
  • Aalapanai
  • Neyar Viruppam
  • Suttu Viral

His poems combine modern imagery, love, philosophy and social observation.

Aalapanai received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

His work also shows the influence of compact lyric and ghazal-like emotional expression where relevant.

Mu. Metha

Mu. Metha is closely associated with modern Tamil free verse.

Important works include:

  • Kanneer Pookkal
  • Oorvalam
  • Manachiragu
  • Velicham Veliye Illai

His poetry uses accessible language and frequently deals with social life, love, poverty and human relationships.

His accessible free verse connects urban experience with love, poverty and ordinary human relationships.

Sirpi Balasubramaniam

Important works include:

  • Oru Gramathu Nadhi
  • Nilavuppoo
  • Sarppa Yagam
  • Mouna Mayakkangal

His poetry is associated with rural life, nature, social concerns and modern imagery.

He also contributed through translation, literary scholarship and the modern reinterpretation of rural experience.

Inkulab, Vairamuthu and Other Contemporary Poets

Inkulab and Vairamuthu illustrate political protest, anti-caste thought, rural imagery and the widening public reach of contemporary poetry.

Inkulab

Original name: Shahul Hameed

Pen name: Inkulab

His writings focus on:

  • Social equality
  • Caste oppression
  • Labour
  • Political resistance
  • Religious harmony

Important works include:

  • Ovvoru Pullaiyum
  • Kanmani Rajam
  • Avvai

His play Avvai reinterprets the traditional image of the woman poet Avvaiyar.

His revolutionary writing reflects Marxist thought, anti-caste politics, human-rights concerns and political theatre.

Vairamuthu

Important literary works include:

  • Vaigarai Megangal
  • Thiruthi Ezhuthiya Theerppugal
  • Kallikkattu Ithikasam
  • Karuvachi Kaviyam
  • Thanneer Desam
  • Moondram Ulaga Por

Kallikkattu Ithikasam deals with communities displaced by the construction of the Vaigai dam and received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2003.

Vairamuthu received the 60th Jnanpith Award for 2025, making him the third Tamil recipient after Akilan and Jayakanthan. The award was conferred in July 2026.

His wider career includes modern poetry, rural imagery, social themes, novels and film lyrics.

Other Contemporary Poets
Erode Tamilanban

Associated with socially engaged modern poetry, Tamil identity and public literary activity.

Meera

Associated with modern free verse, social feeling and accessible poetic expression.

Kalapriya

Known for modern imagery, inward experience and distinctive free-verse expression.

Vikramadityan

Associated with contemporary lyric poetry, urban experience and individual voice.

Devadevan

Known for reflective contemporary poetry engaging nature, self and philosophical experience.

Manushyaputhiran

Associated with contemporary poetry, cultural debate, publishing and modern public discourse.

Jayakanthan and Sundara Ramasamy

Jayakanthan and Sundara Ramasamy shaped mature post-Independence fiction through social realism, modernism, criticism and experimentation.

Jayakanthan

Jayakanthan wrote novels, novellas, short stories and essays.

Important works include:

  • Sila Nerangalil Sila Manithargal
  • Oru Nadigai Nadagam Parkiral
  • Oru Manithan Oru Veedu Oru Ulagam
  • Unnaipol Oruvan
  • Yaarukkaga Azhudhan
  • Parisukku Po

Sila Nerangalil Sila Manithargal received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

Jayakanthan received the Jnanpith Award for 2002 for his contribution to Tamil literature.

His mature post-Independence writing foregrounds urban working-class life, marginalised communities, women, psychological conflict and social realism; he was also involved in cinema.

Sundara Ramasamy

Important novels include:

  • Oru Puliyamarathin Kathai
  • J. J. Sila Kurippugal
  • Kuzhanthaigal Pengal Aangal

Important short-story collections include:

  • Akkaraich Cheemaiyil
  • Pallam

Sundara Ramasamy wrote poetry under the pen name Pasuvayya.

He founded the literary and cultural journal Kalachuvadu in 1988.

His mature work combines modernism, experimental narrative, literary criticism and institution-building through Kalachuvadu.

Ashokamitran, T. Janakiraman and Ki. Rajanarayanan

Ashokamitran, T. Janakiraman and Ki. Rajanarayanan developed minimalist urban, psychological-cultural and Karisal regional traditions.

Ashokamitran

Original name: Jagadisa Thyagarajan

Pen name: Ashokamitran

Important works include:

  • Pathinettavathu Atchakkodu
  • Thanneer
  • Karaindha Nizhalgal
  • Manasarovar
  • Otran
  • Appavin Snegithar

His works frequently portray:

  • Chennai’s middle-class life
  • Cinema-studio workers
  • Urban isolation
  • Ordinary individuals
  • Subtle humour

He also served as an editor of Kanaiyazhi.

His minimalist prose derives much of its power from understatement, close observation and the film-studio experience.

T. Janakiraman

Important novels include:

  • Mogamul
  • Amma Vandhal
  • Marappasu
  • Semparuthi
  • Uyirthen

His fiction is noted for:

  • Music
  • Emotional relationships
  • Women characters
  • Family conflicts
  • Refined prose

He also edited Kanaiyazhi during a later phase.

His wider prose also includes short stories and travel writing alongside psychologically sensitive novels.

Ki. Rajanarayanan

Popular abbreviation: Ki. Ra.

Region associated: Karisal region

Important works include:

  • Gopalla Gramam
  • Gopallapurathu Makkal
  • Karisal Kattu Kaduthasi
  • Nattuppura Kathaik Kalanjiyam

Ki. Ra. used the spoken language and oral traditions of the Karisal region.

Gopallapurathu Makkal received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

He played an important role in recording Tamil folk tales and regional vocabulary.

His work helped establish Karisal literature as a major regional tradition grounded in oral narrative and spoken vocabulary.

Rajam Krishnan, Indira Parthasarathy and Sa. Kandasamy

Rajam Krishnan, Indira Parthasarathy and Sa. Kandasamy connected social research, history, political criticism and changing rural–urban life.

Rajam Krishnan

Important novels include:

  • Verukku Neer
  • Kurinjithen
  • Karippu Manigal
  • Alaivaai Karaiyil
  • Mannagaththu Poonthuligal

Her novels examine:

  • Women’s lives
  • Agricultural workers
  • Fisherfolk
  • Salt-pan workers
  • Child labour
  • Female infanticide
  • Social inequality

Rajam Krishnan is recognised as an important Tamil social novelist.

Her field-based social research gives many novels a documentary-realist quality.

Indira Parthasarathy

Important novels include:

  • Kuruthipunal
  • Thandhira Bhoomi
  • Vendar Bhoomi
  • Helikoptergal Keezhe Irangivittana

Important plays include:

  • Aurangzeb
  • Nandan Kathai
  • Mazhai
  • Kongai Thee

Kuruthipunal received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

Kongai Thee reinterprets the Kannagi narrative, while Nandan Kathai revisits the story of Nandanar.

His work links history, urban alienation, political criticism, fiction and theatre.

Sa. Kandasamy

Important works include:

  • Chayavanam
  • Avan Aanathu
  • Vicharanai Commission
  • Tholaindhu Ponavargal

His fiction deals with rural transformation, administration, human relationships and political power.

Vicharanai Commission received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

He also engaged with documentary practice and visual-art interests while examining social transformation and power.

Prapanchan, Ponneelan and D. Selvaraj

Prapanchan, Ponneelan and D. Selvaraj used colonial history, Marxist realism, labour and social reform as major fictional concerns.

Prapanchan

Original name: S. Vaidyalingam

Pen name: Prapanchan

Important works include:

  • Vaanam Vasappadum
  • Mahanadhi
  • Manudam Vellum
  • Kanniral Kaappom

His historical novels frequently use the background of French colonial Puducherry.

Vaanam Vasappadum received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

His fiction combines Puducherry’s colonial history with social realism and historical reconstruction.

Ponneelan

Important works include:

  • Karisal
  • Puthiya Darisanangal
  • Marupakkam
  • Ootrile Malarndhathu

His fiction deals with:

  • Rural Tamil Nadu
  • Land relations
  • Labour
  • Social reform
  • Political movements

Puthiya Darisanangal received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

Marxist influence, labour, education and social reform are recurring concerns in his writing.

D. Selvaraj

Important works include:

  • Malarum Sarugum
  • Theneer
  • Thol

His novels focus on workers, caste oppression and labour conditions.

Thol deals with leather-industry workers and received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

His working-class fiction includes plantation and industrial labour, trade-union struggles and Marxist realism.

Poomani, Nanjil Nadan and Imayam

Poomani, Nanjil Nadan and Imayam examine regional society, caste, migration, violence, marginal lives and historical memory.

Poomani

Important novels include:

  • Piragu
  • Vekkai
  • Naivedhyam
  • Varappugal
  • Agnaadi

Vekkai centres on caste violence, revenge and rural life.

Agnaadi is a large historical novel depicting marginalised communities and received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2014.

His fiction uses southern Tamil regional language to examine caste, violence, rural society and historical memory.

Nanjil Nadan

Important works include:

  • Thalaikeezh Vigitangal
  • Enbilathanai Veyil Kayum
  • Mithavai
  • Soodiya Poo Soodarka

His works are associated with the Nanjil region, migration, agriculture and changing social relations.

Soodiya Poo Soodarka received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

Migration, rural transformation, satire and detailed social observation shape his Nanjil-region writing.

Imayam

Important works include:

  • Koveru Kazhuthaigal
  • Arumugam
  • Sedal
  • Pethavan
  • Sellatha Panam

Koveru Kazhuthaigal portrays the life of a washer-community family.

Sedal deals with a woman dedicated to a religious institution.

Sellatha Panam received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2020.

His realist narratives examine caste relations, women and marginalised rural communities; his specific role in Dalit literary development is noted separately in Topic 13.

Perumal Murugan, Jeyamohan and S. Ramakrishnan

Perumal Murugan, Jeyamohan and S. Ramakrishnan connect regional culture, myth, digital publication, folklore, travel and contemporary narrative experimentation.

Perumal Murugan

Important works include:

  • Eru Veyil
  • Koolamadari
  • Kanganam
  • Madhorubhagan
  • Poonachi
  • Aalavayan
  • Arthanari

His fiction is strongly associated with:

  • Kongu region
  • Rural communities
  • Land and caste
  • Folk beliefs
  • Marriage and childlessness
  • Regional vocabulary

Madhorubhagan is known in English as One Part Woman.

His wider work includes poetry and lexicography, especially the documentation of Kongu regional vocabulary and folk traditions.

Jeyamohan

Important works include:

  • Rubber
  • Vishnupuram
  • Kaadu
  • Ezhaam Ulagam
  • Aram
  • Venmurasu

Venmurasu is an extensive modern Tamil reworking of the Mahabharata tradition.

His writings include novels, short stories, essays, philosophy, criticism and screenwriting.

Digital publication became important to the circulation of his large-scale Venmurasu project.

S. Ramakrishnan

Important works include:

  • Nedunkuruthi
  • Yaamam
  • Upa Paandavam
  • Urupasi
  • Sancharam
  • Desanthiri

Sancharam centres on the lives of Nadaswaram musicians and received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

His writing also spans travel, folklore, cinema, history and oral storytelling traditions.

Su. Venkatesan, Cho. Dharman and Devibharathi

Su. Venkatesan, Cho. Dharman and Devibharathi use research, environmental and social conflict, psychology and experimental narrative.

Su. Venkatesan

Important novels include:

  • Kaaval Kottam
  • Veera Yuga Nayagan Velpari

Kaaval Kottam deals with the historical development of Madurai and the Kaval system.

It received the Sahitya Akademi Award.

Velpari is a historical novel based on the Sangam-age chief Pari.

His research-based historical fiction connects Madurai, the Kaval system and Kallar social history.

Cho. Dharman

Important works include:

  • Koogai
  • Sool
  • Pathimoonraavathu Maiyavaadi

His works portray rural southern Tamil Nadu, caste relations, water scarcity, agriculture and marginalised communities.

Sool received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2019.

Environmental decline, water scarcity and the lives of Dalit and marginalised Karisal communities are recurring concerns.

Devibharathi

Important works include:

  • Nizhalin Thanimai
  • Natraj Maharaj
  • Neervazhippadum

Neervazhippadum received the Sahitya Akademi Award for 2023.

His contemporary narratives use psychological conflict, violence, power and experimental form.

Dalit Literature and Its Major Writers

Dalit literature records lived caste experience, assertion, autobiography, criticism and the recovery of suppressed social histories.

Growth of Tamil Dalit Writing

Tamil Dalit literature became especially prominent from the late twentieth century.

Important writers include:

  • K. Daniel
  • P. Sivakami
  • Bama
  • Raj Gauthaman
  • D. Selvaraj
  • Azhagiya Periyavan
  • Imayam
  • Cho. Dharman

The literature records caste oppression, labour, religious discrimination, community memory and struggles for dignity.

Tamil Dalit writing developed through lived experience, autobiography, fiction, poetry, criticism, movement publications and the recovery of suppressed histories.

Dalit journals and alternative literary spaces helped connect anti-caste politics with new narrative and critical forms.

K. Daniel

K. Daniel was a Sri Lankan Tamil writer closely associated with anti-untouchability movements.

Important novels include:

  • Panchamar
  • Govindan
  • Adimaigal
  • Thanneer

His works portray caste oppression among Sri Lankan Tamils and are important early contributions to Tamil Dalit fiction.

P. Sivakami

P. Sivakami wrote under the pen name Nithya during part of her literary career.

Important works include:

  • Pazhaiyana Kazhithalum
  • Anandhayi
  • Kurukku Vettu
  • Kadaisi Mandhar

Pazhaiyana Kazhithalum was first published in 1988 and is widely identified as the first Tamil novel written by a Dalit woman.

Bama

Name: Bama Faustina

Major work: Karukku

Publication: 1992

Important works include:

  • Karukku
  • Sangati
  • Vanmam
  • Kusumbukkaran
  • Oru Thathavum Erumaiyum

Karukku is an autobiographical work dealing with Dalit Christian life, caste discrimination, religious institutions and education.

Sangati concentrates particularly on the lives and voices of Dalit women.

Vanmam examines conflict between two oppressed communities.

Karukku is regarded as a landmark in contemporary Tamil Dalit literature.

Raj Gauthaman

Raj Gauthaman is associated with:

  • Dalit literary criticism
  • Cultural history
  • Fiction
  • Autobiographical writing

Important works include:

  • Siluvairaj Charithiram
  • Kaalachumai
  • Dalit Panpaadu

His criticism re-examines Tamil literary and cultural history from marginalised perspectives.

Other Major Dalit Literary Voices
Azhagiya Periyavan

Associated with fiction centred on caste, dignity, memory and marginalised rural experience.

Ravikumar

Associated with Dalit criticism, translation, political writing and alternative publishing.

Sukirtharani

Her role in Dalit literature lies in poetry connecting caste, labour, the female body and social exclusion; her broader feminist contribution is treated in Topic 14.

Cho. Dharman and Imayam

Both are important to discussions of marginalised communities and caste, but their complete biographies and work lists remain in Topics 10 and 12.

K. A. Gunasekaran

Associated with Dalit autobiography, theatre, folk performance and the documentation of lived caste experience.

Abimani

Associated with contemporary anti-caste and Dalit literary expression.

Women’s Writing and Feminist Voices

Women’s and feminist writing examines gendered power, body, labour, caste, family, sexuality and personal freedom without treating all women’s writing as identical.

Scope of Women’s and Feminist Writing

Women’s writing records diverse experiences of family, marriage, labour, body, caste, domestic violence, sexuality and personal freedom.

Writing by a woman is not automatically feminist; feminist writing explicitly questions unequal gender structures, representation and power.

Ambai

Original name: C. S. Lakshmi

Pen name: Ambai

Important works include:

  • Siragukal Muriyum
  • Veettin Mulaiyil Oru Samayalarai
  • Kaattil Oru Maan
  • Vattrum Eriyin Meengal
  • Sivappu Kazhuthudan Oru Pachai Paravai

Her fiction deals with women’s bodies, domestic labour, marriage, music, travel and independence.

Sivappu Kazhuthudan Oru Pachai Paravai received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2021.

Sivasankari

Important works include:

  • 47 Natkal
  • Oru Manithanin Kathai
  • Palangal
  • Avan
  • Verillatha Marangal

Her novels address alcoholism, family relationships, migration, women’s lives and social problems.

Salma

Original name: Rajathi

Pen name: Salma

Important poetry collections include:

  • Oru Maalaiyum Innoru Maalaiyum
  • Pachchai Devathai

Important novels include:

  • Irandam Jaamangalin Kathai
  • Manamiyangal

Her works portray women’s lives, confinement, sexuality and patriarchy, particularly within Tamil Muslim social settings.

Kutti Revathi

Kutti Revathi is a poet, writer and medical practitioner.

Important works include:

  • Poonaiyai Pol Alaiyum Velicham
  • Mulaigal
  • Thanimaiyin Aayiram Irakkaigal
  • Udalin Kathavu

The poetry collection Mulaigal, published in 2002, generated a major debate about women’s bodies and language in Tamil poetry.

Sukirtharani

Important poetry collections include:

  • Kaipattri En Kanavu Kel
  • Iravu Mirugam
  • Avalai Mozhipeyarthal
  • Theendapadatha Mutham

Her poetry addresses:

  • Caste
  • Women’s bodies
  • Labour
  • Desire
  • Social exclusion
  • Dalit women’s experience
Other Feminist and Contemporary Women Poets
Malathi Maitri

Associated with feminist poetry, the female body, sexuality and resistance to patriarchal language.

Vennila

Associated with contemporary women’s poetry and writing on personal and social experience.

Thamizhachi Thangapandian

Associated with contemporary poetry, women’s experience, place, memory and Tamil cultural expression.

Uma Maheswari

Associated with contemporary fiction and poetry centred on women, interior experience and social relationships.

Sri Lankan and Diaspora Tamil Literature

Sri Lankan and diaspora Tamil literature documents war, displacement, plantation experience, global migration, memory and language preservation.

Sri Lankan Tamil Writing

Important Sri Lankan Tamil writers include:

  • Mahakavi
  • Kasi Anandan
  • K. Daniel
  • S. Ponnuthurai
  • A. Muttulingam
  • Cheran
  • V. I. S. Jayapalan
  • Shobasakthi

Major themes include:

  • Ethnic conflict
  • Displacement
  • Migration
  • War
  • Refugee life
  • Memory
  • Homeland

The field also includes plantation Tamil experience and global Tamil migration to Malaysia, Singapore, Europe, Canada, Australia and Gulf countries.

Diaspora writing examines language preservation, identity, intergenerational memory and cultural negotiation beyond the homeland.

Cheran

Cheran is an important Sri Lankan Tamil poet.

Important collections include:

  • Irandavathu Sooriya Uthayam
  • Yaman
  • Kaanal Vari
  • Kaadaatru

His poems deal with war, exile, memory, loss and displaced Tamil identity.

A. Muttulingam

A. Muttulingam is known mainly for short stories.

Important works include:

  • Akka
  • Maharajavin Rail Vandi
  • Digadachakkaram
  • Amerikakari

His stories frequently portray migration, cultural encounters, humour and diaspora life.

Shobasakthi

Important works include:

  • Gorilla
  • M
  • Box

His fiction draws on war, militant politics, migration, caste and refugee experience.

Gorilla is one of the best-known contemporary novels concerning the Sri Lankan Tamil conflict and diaspora.

Other Sri Lankan and Diaspora Voices
Murugaiyan

Associated with Sri Lankan Tamil poetry, modern literary expression and the island’s social experience.

Dominic Jeeva

Associated with Sri Lankan Tamil short stories, progressive writing and the journal Mallikai.

S. Ponnuthurai

A major Sri Lankan Tamil fiction writer associated with social and psychological narratives.

M. Thalayasingam

Associated with Sri Lankan Tamil criticism, fiction and intellectual debate.

V. I. S. Jayapalan

Associated with poetry of exile, identity, homeland and displacement.

Rajani Thiranagama

Her writing and testimony are relevant to the documentation of war, human rights and Sri Lankan social conflict.

Contemporary Tamil Drama

Contemporary Tamil theatre combines experimental staging, folk adaptation, street performance, political critique, anti-caste drama and women’s theatre.

Na. Muthusamy

Na. Muthusamy was a major modern Tamil playwright.

Important plays include:

  • Narkalikarar
  • Suvarottigal
  • England
  • Kaalam Kaalamaaga

He founded Koothu-P-Pattarai, an important modern theatre organisation.

His drama combined traditional Koothu practices with experimental modern theatre.

Komal Swaminathan

Important plays include:

  • Thanneer Thanneer
  • Nawab Narkali
  • Sorgga Bhoomi
  • Yuddha Kandam

Thanneer Thanneer deals with drought, water scarcity, bureaucracy and political neglect.

It was later adapted as a film directed by K. Balachander.

Indira Parthasarathy’s Plays

Important plays include:

  • Aurangzeb
  • Nandan Kathai
  • Mazhai
  • Kongai Thee

Kongai Thee reinterprets Silappadikaram.

Nandan Kathai re-examines the Nandanar tradition through caste and social power.

Experimental, Political and Street Theatre

Contemporary theatre uses experimental staging, folk-theatre adaptation, political performance, street theatre, anti-caste drama and women’s theatre.

Pralayan

Associated with political and street theatre, collective performance and socially engaged drama.

Mangai

Associated with feminist theatre, women’s performance, criticism and alternative stage practice.

Murugaboopathi

Associated with experimental Tamil theatre, performance research and new stage languages.

Inkulab

His dramatic writing, including Avvai, links political protest, gender reinterpretation and anti-caste thought.

Little Magazines and Contemporary Literary Journals

Little magazines and digital platforms create alternative spaces for modernism, translation, criticism, Dalit and feminist writing and new literary voices.

Small literary journals played an important role in modern poetry, short stories, translation and new critical movements.

Little magazines differ from mainstream commercial journals through smaller circulation, editorial independence and a stronger role in experimentation, criticism, translation and movement-based writing.

They created alternative spaces for modernism, Dalit writing, feminist writing, political debate and new writers.

Kasadathapara

Associated with experimental modern poetry, criticism and the little-magazine tradition.

Uyirmai

Associated with contemporary literature, publishing, criticism and public cultural debate.

Subamangala

An influential literary magazine supporting fiction, interviews, criticism and cultural discussion.

Dalit

Associated with Dalit literary and political discourse and the creation of anti-caste publishing space.

Nirapirigai

Associated with critical debate, social theory, identity and alternative intellectual writing.

Sol Puthithu

Associated with contemporary creative writing, criticism and newer literary voices.

Digital Literary Platforms

Online magazines, blogs and digital publishing widened access to poetry, fiction, criticism, archives and diaspora participation.

Awards and Literary Categories

The Sahitya Akademi Award recognises an individual work in a recognised Indian language, while the Jnanpith Award recognises an author’s major literary contribution at the national level.

Other forms of recognition include Saraswati Samman, national and state literary awards, translation prizes and institutional honours. Award lists must be read with the work, year and literary category together.

Translations and Global Recognition

Translations carry Tamil poetry, fiction, autobiography and criticism into other Indian and world languages.

International publication, university study, literary festivals and translation awards expand recognition beyond Tamil Nadu and connect Tamil Nadu, Sri Lankan and diaspora writing with global readers.

A translated title must not be confused with the original Tamil title or treated as a separate original work.

High-Yield Distinctions
  • Ezhuthu was founded by C. S. Chellappa; Kalachuvadu was founded by Sundara Ramasamy.
  • Pasuvayya was the poetic pen name of Sundara Ramasamy.
  • Ashokamitran’s original name was Jagadisa Thyagarajan.
  • Ambai’s original name is C. S. Lakshmi.
  • Inkulab’s original name was Shahul Hameed.
  • Pramil’s original name was Dharmu Sivaramu.
  • Nakulan’s original name was T. K. Doraiswamy.
  • Karukku was written by Bama; Pazhaiyana Kazhithalum was written by P. Sivakami.
  • Koveru Kazhuthaigal was written by Imayam; Vekkai was written by Poomani.
  • Madhorubhagan was written by Perumal Murugan.
  • J. J. Sila Kurippugal was written by Sundara Ramasamy.
  • Pathinettavathu Atchakkodu was written by Ashokamitran.
  • Thanneer Thanneer is a play by Komal Swaminathan; Thanneer is a novel by Ashokamitran.
  • Koothu-P-Pattarai was founded by Na. Muthusamy.
  • Agnaadi received the 2014 Sahitya Akademi Award; Sellatha Panam received the 2020 award.
  • Akilan, Jayakanthan and Vairamuthu are the three Tamil Jnanpith recipients as of July 2026.
  • Modern Tamil Literature in Chapter 7 emphasises printing, literary firsts and the formation of modern genres; Contemporary Tamil Literature emphasises post-Independence maturity, later movements and twenty-first-century writing.
  • Traditional poetry follows established metrical systems; Puthu Kavithai uses free verse, flexible lineation and modern speech.
  • Na. Pichamurthy is a pioneer of Tamil free verse; later poets developed distinct modernist, social, regional and political directions.
  • Jayakanthan is strongly associated with social realism and marginalised urban lives; Sundara Ramasamy with modernism, experimentation and criticism.
  • Ashokamitran is noted for minimalist urban prose; T. Janakiraman for psychological relationships, music and refined prose.
  • Ki. Rajanarayanan is central to Karisal oral and regional tradition; Poomani uses southern regional fiction to examine caste, violence and historical memory.
  • Social realism represents concrete social relations and material conditions; modernism often foregrounds form, perception, alienation and experiment.
  • Regional literature is defined by place, speech and local culture; Dalit literature is shaped by anti-caste experience, assertion and the recovery of suppressed histories.
  • Writing about Dalit communities is not automatically Dalit literature; authorship, perspective, lived experience and anti-caste literary location matter.
  • Women’s writing includes diverse writing by women; feminist writing explicitly interrogates gendered power and inequality.
  • Tamil Nadu writing and Sri Lankan Tamil literature share a language but arise from distinct histories, including civil war, exile and diaspora.
  • Little magazines prioritise experimentation and alternative debate; mainstream commercial journals generally target wider circulation and popular readership.
  • Modern drama in Chapter 7 covers company theatre and stage reform; contemporary theatre covers experimental, street, feminist and political performance.
  • Sahitya Akademi Award is commonly linked to a specific work and year; Jnanpith Award recognises major literary contribution at the national level.
